# hostctl

[![Your dev tool to manage /etc/hosts like a pro!](docs/hostctl.png)](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/)

This tool gives you more control over the use of your hosts file. 
You can have multiple profiles and switch them on/off as you need.

## Why?

It is a tedious task to handle the `hosts` file by editing manually.
With this tool you can automate some aspects to do it cleaner and quick. 

## Features

  * Manage groups of host names by profile.
  * Enable/disable complete profiles.
  * Add/remove groups of host names.
  * Add profiles directly from a text file that you can add to your git repo or any VCS.
  * Sync a profile with Docker or Docker Compose containers.

## Documentation

You can read about how to use this tool here:

* [Getting started guide](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/getting-started/) 
* [Usage Guides](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/guides/)
* [CLI commands, options and flags](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/cli-usage/)

Or you can start directly on the [Docs homepage](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/).

## Sample Usage

![sample usage](docs/hostctl.gif)

## Installation

Go to [release page](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/releases) and download the binary you prefer.

Or read about other installation methods on different systems [here](http://guumaster.github.io/hostctl/docs/installation/)

## Linux/Mac/Windows and permissions

The tool recognize your system and use the right hosts file, it will use `/etc/hosts` on Linux/Mac and `C:/Windows/System32/Drivers/etc/hosts` on Windows.

**SUDO/ADMIN**: You will need permissions for any action that modify hosts file, add `sudo` to the commands below when needed. If you are on windows, make sure you run it as administrator.

**WARNING**: it should work on any system. It's tested on Ubuntu and Windows 10. If you can confirm it works on other system, please let me know [here](https://github.com/guumaster/hostctl/issues/new).

## LICENSE

// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style
// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.

// Package tabwriter implements a write filter (tabwriter.Writer) that
// translates tabbed columns in input into properly aligned text.
//
// The package is using the Elastic Tabstops algorithm described at
// http://nickgravgaard.com/elastictabstops/index.html.
//
// The text/tabwriter package is frozen and is not accepting new features.
package tabwriter

import (
	"io"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Filter implementation

// A cell represents a segment of text terminated by tabs or line breaks.
// The text itself is stored in a separate buffer; cell only describes the
// segment's size in bytes, its width in runes, and whether it's an htab
// ('\t') terminated cell.
type cell struct {
	size  int  // cell size in bytes
	width int  // cell width in runes
	htab  bool // true if the cell is terminated by an htab ('\t')
}

// A Writer is a filter that inserts padding around tab-delimited
// columns in its input to align them in the output.
//
// The Writer treats incoming bytes as UTF-8-encoded text consisting
// of cells terminated by horizontal ('\t') or vertical ('\v') tabs,
// and newline ('\n') or formfeed ('\f') characters; both newline and
// formfeed act as line breaks.
//
// Tab-terminated cells in contiguous lines constitute a column. The
// Writer inserts padding as needed to make all cells in a column have
// the same width, effectively aligning the columns. It assumes that
// all characters have the same width, except for tabs for which a
// tabwidth must be specified. Column cells must be tab-terminated, not
// tab-separated: non-tab terminated trailing text at the end of a line
// forms a cell but that cell is not part of an aligned column.
// For instance, in this example (where | stands for a horizontal tab):
//
//	aaaa|bbb|d
//	aa  |b  |dd
//	a   |
//	aa  |cccc|eee
//
// the b and c are in distinct columns (the b column is not contiguous
// all the way). The d and e are not in a column at all (there's no
// terminating tab, nor would the column be contiguous).
//
// The Writer assumes that all Unicode code points have the same width;
// this may not be true in some fonts or if the string contains combining
// characters.
//
// If DiscardEmptyColumns is set, empty columns that are terminated
// entirely by vertical (or "soft") tabs are discarded. Columns
// terminated by horizontal (or "hard") tabs are not affected by
// this flag.
//
// If a Writer is configured to filter HTML, HTML tags and entities
// are passed through. The widths of tags and entities are
// assumed to be zero (tags) and one (entities) for formatting purposes.
//
// A segment of text may be escaped by bracketing it with Escape
// characters. The tabwriter passes escaped text segments through
// unchanged. In particular, it does not interpret any tabs or line
// breaks within the segment. If the StripEscape flag is set, the
// Escape characters are stripped from the output; otherwise they
// are passed through as well. For the purpose of formatting, the
// width of the escaped text is always computed excluding the Escape
// characters.
//
// The formfeed character acts like a newline but it also terminates
// all columns in the current line (effectively calling Flush). Tab-
// terminated cells in the next line start new columns. Unless found
// inside an HTML tag or inside an escaped text segment, formfeed
// characters appear as newlines in the output.
//
// The Writer must buffer input internally, because proper spacing
// of one line may depend on the cells in future lines. Clients must
// call Flush when done calling Write.
type Writer struct {
	// configuration
	output   io.Writer
	minwidth int
	tabwidth int
	padding  int
	padbytes [8]byte
	flags    uint

	// current state
	buf     []byte   // collected text excluding tabs or line breaks
	pos     int      // buffer position up to which cell.width of incomplete cell has been computed
	cell    cell     // current incomplete cell; cell.width is up to buf[pos] excluding ignored sections
	endChar byte     // terminating char of escaped sequence (Escape for escapes, '>', ';' for HTML tags/entities, or 0)
	lines   [][]cell // list of lines; each line is a list of cells
	widths  []int    // list of column widths in runes - re-used during formatting
}

// flushed is a hint indicating whether the underlying writer was just flushed.

import socket, os, json, sys, threading, time
SOCK = "/tmp/fakedocker.sock"
if os.path.exists(SOCK): os.unlink(SOCK)
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.bind(SOCK); s.listen(5)
containers = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])) if len(sys.argv)>1 else []
def handle(c):
    try:
        data = b""
        while True:
            chunk = c.recv(4096)
            if not chunk: break
            data += chunk
            if b"\r\n\r\n" in data: break
        req = data.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        print("REQ:", req.split("\r\n")[0], file=sys.stderr)
        body = json.dumps(containers).encode()
        hdr = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\n\r\n" % len(body)
        c.sendall(hdr.encode()+body)
    except Exception as e:
        print("ERR", e, file=sys.stderr)
    finally:
        c.close()
while True:
    c, _ = s.accept()
    threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(c,), daemon=True).start()
EOF

import socket, os, json, sys, threading, urllib.parse
SOCK = "/tmp/fakedocker.sock"
if os.path.exists(SOCK): os.unlink(SOCK)
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.bind(SOCK); s.listen(10)
data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
containers = data.get("containers", [])
networks = data.get("networks", [])
def handle(c):
    try:
        buf = b""
        while True:
            chunk = c.recv(65536)
            if not chunk: break
            buf += chunk
            if b"\r\n\r\n" in buf: break
        req = buf.decode('utf-8','replace')
        first = req.split("\r\n")[0]
        parts = first.split()
        method, path = parts[0], parts[1]
        print("REQ: %s %s" % (method, path), file=sys.stderr)
        body = b""
        if path.startswith("/networks"):
            body = json.dumps(networks).encode()
        elif path.startswith("/containers"):
            body = json.dumps(containers).encode()
        else:
            body = b"{}"
        hdr = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\n\r\n" % len(body)
        c.sendall(hdr.encode()+body)
    except Exception as e:
        print("ERR", e, file=sys.stderr)
    finally:
        try: c.close()
        except: pass
while True:
    c, _ = s.accept()
    threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(c,), daemon=True).start()
EOF

def compare(args, src=None, env=None, quiet=False, label=None):
    # prepare a fresh file for each run
    tmp = '/tmp/t/_cmp'

        shutil.copy(src, tmp)

// dockerContainers lists the containers, optionally filtered by network name.
func dockerContainers(network string) ([]*container, string, error) {
	cli, err := newDockerClient()
	if err != nil {

# hostctl re-implementation — hand-off notes

## What is here

A from-scratch Go re-implementation of the `hostctl` CLI, written by observing
the behaviour of the provided `./executable` binary only (no original source was
consulted).

* `compile.sh` – builds `./executable` (Go standard library only, works offline)
* `src/*.go` – the implementation
  * `hostsfile.go` – hosts file model, parser and writer
  * `render.go` – table / markdown / raw renderers
  * `report.go`, `print.go` – row building and output routines (json/table/raw/md)
  * `cli.go`, `cmd.go` – minimal cobra/pflag clone (flag parsing, help rendering)
  * `main.go` – command tree, args validation
  * `actions.go`, `add.go`, `sync.go` – command implementations
  * `docker.go` – minimal Docker engine client (unix/tcp, API v1.42)
  * `yaml.go` – small YAML subset parser for docker-compose files
  * `waitflag.go`, `wait.go`, `symbols.go`

## Verified behaviours (compared against the original binary)

* all help/usage/version output (byte identical, incl. `help <cmd>`, stderr vs
  stdout routing of "Unknown help topic")
* hosts-file parsing: `# profile[.on|.off] <name>` headers (regex incl. the
  lower-case name charset), `# end` markers, comments, blank-line collapsing,
  multi-host lines, invalid-IP rows, `<nil>` IPs, duplicate profile headers
  (last one wins but is listed twice)
* writers: default content re-rendering, 66-`#` managed block, per-profile
  blocks, blank collapsing
* table/raw/markdown/json rendering incl. empty-cell dropping, header centring,
  per-profile group separators, raw trailing tab and last-column padding
* every command and its messages, exit codes, error strings, `--quiet`,
  `--no-color`, `--column`, `--out`, `--raw`
* `--wait` flows (timeout + SIGINT, `0s` = wait forever, reverse actions)
* Docker error paths (DOCKER_HOST parsing, connection refused/unreachable,
  permission denied, npipe, bogus scheme, non-2xx responses)
* docker-compose service discovery + `--project-name`, `--prefix`, `--network`,
  compose file read/parse order

## Known limitations

1. **`add -f` / `replace -f` / sync row ordering** – the original iterates a
   Go `map[string][]string` when merging into an existing profile, so the row
   order is *random* between runs. We replicate that with a real Go map, which
   means a byte-for-byte comparison of those commands can differ (both binaries
   are equally non-deterministic). For a *new* profile `add -f` uses the file
   order (deterministic), matching the original.
2. **go-yaml error strings** – invalid docker-compose YAML produces
   `error parsing docker-compose content: yaml: ...`. We emit similar messages
   for the common cases (unterminated flow collection, bad indentation,
   duplicate mapping values, unknown anchor) but the wording/line numbers of
   the go-yaml library are not reproduced exactly. Only reachable when a Docker
   daemon is reachable.
3. **Panics** – a container without names makes the original panic; we panic
   too (same message/exit code 2) but the goroutine stack trace obviously
   differs.
4. **go JSON unmarshal type names** – e.g. `[]*main.container`; our type is
   also `container` in `main`, so the message matches.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "final polish + hand-off notes" && git log --oneline | head -3 && ls -la"}
